articles.title: It’s Officially the End of an Era for HBO’s The Last of Us
articles.summary: It's officially the end of the road for The Last of Us at HBO. While the upcoming third season was already set to conclude the show's adaptation of the second game in Naughty Dog's acclaimed PlayStation series, there was some hope it could continue on after.
body: Casey Bloys, chairman and CEO of HBO and Max content, shared several updates on upcoming projects with Deadline in September, following a successful night at the Emmys for the company. That included The Last of Us, with Bloys saying that, "Craig [Mazin] has planned it as the final season."
Mazin is the co-creator and showrunner of the series. After The Last of Us, he's moving on to create a Dungeons & Dragons show, a sequel to Baldur's Gate 3, for HBO.

After adapting the first game in the first season of the show, HBO split The Last of Us Part 2 across two seasons to reflect the game's dual protagonists. Season 2 tells the story of Ellie's (Bella Ramsey) quest for revenge following the death of Joel (Pedro Pascal) and her hunt for Abby (Kaitlyn Dever). Season 3 will flip the perspective, retelling the same period of time as season 2 from Abby's point of view. This will also introduce the character of Lev, played by Michelle Mao.
points: It's officially the end of the road for The Last of Us at HBO.

articles.title: Amazon Has an Asus ROG Flow Z13 Ultra-Portable Gaming Laptop for (Way) Below $2,000 for Black Friday
articles.summary: For Black Friday, Amazon is offering the lowest price I've seen on ASUS' powerful ultraportable gaming convertible. You can pick up a brand new Asus ROG Flow Z13 gaming laptop with 32GB of RAM for just $1,699.99 with free shipping after a $400 off discount.
body: The Asus ROG Flow Z13 is a 13.4" 2-in-1 convertible laptop that weighs in at only 2.65 pounds without the detachable keyboard. That's about one pound heavier than the Xbox Ally X handheld, which weighs in at 1.6 pounds. With the keyboard, the Z13 weighs about 3.5 pounds. A premium laptop deserves premium build quality, and the Flow Z13 doesn't disappoint with a blacked out CNC aluminum alloy chassis and Corning Gorilla Glass Victus screen protection.

This particular configuration is equipped with a 13.4" 2560x1600 180Hz IPS display, AMD Ryzen AI Max 390 CPU with AMD Radeon 8050S iGPU, 32GB of LPDDR5X-8000Mhz RAM, and a 1TB SSD. This is less powerful than the highest end ROG Flow Z13, which comes equipped with a Ryzen AI Max 395 CPU with 8060S iGPU, but it's also far less expensive (currently the least expensive model is $2,100 ). The Radeon 8050S is more powerful than the Ryzen Z2 Extreme APU found in the highest-end handheld gaming PCs like the ROG Xbox Ally X.

articles.title: Marvel's Iron Man might be planning to rear its head at The Game Awards, if EA Motive's updated website is any indication
articles.summary: EA Motive's Iron Man game has been quietly cooking away for a few years now, but don't worry. The wait to finally, officially see the superhero romp in action might be over soon, at least if the developer's updated website - two weeks before The Game Awards, no less - is any indication.
body: Redditors today noticed that EA Motive's official website got a little makeover recently. It's not clear when exactly the tweaks were pushed through, but the Wayback Machine makes clear that it's definitely been updated.
A new website look is by no means confirmation of an imminent announcement, of course, but there are a few other bits of evidence that certainly point in that direction.

For one, The Game Awards 2026 will air on Disney Plus for the very first time, alongside all the other platforms you're used to. "As the evening unfolds, viewers can expect major announcements and surprises from some of Disney's most anticipated titles in gaming," the film studio said earlier this month.
Kingdom Hearts 4, Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra and more are definitely possible, too. Turmoil at Marvel's Blade developer Arkane Lyon makes that one a tricker guess, however.

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering Designer Reveals 2026’s 11 Best New Commanders
articles.summary: With 2026 delivering a packed release schedule for Magic: The Gathering exploring classic planes and several Universes Beyond crossovers, Commander players have had plenty of exciting new legends to build around.
body: When Polygon spoke with Magic: The Gathering Principal Designer Gavin Verhey about the year's lineup at MagicCon: Atlanta 2026, he walked through each major release to highlight what he considers some of 2026’s most powerful Commanders. Rather than focus strictly on raw power ceilings, Verhey pointed toward the legends that spark creative brewing, surprising table politics, and memorable gameplay moments across every 2026 release. Here's a look at this year's 11 best Commanders in the order they were released.

We all love abilities that trigger when something enters the battlefield, don’t we? Well, Maralen, Fae Ascendant takes that to the tenth degree by bridging two of Lorwyn 's most recognizable kindred types into a nimble value engine that’s entirely too fun to abuse. Whenever Maralen or another elf or faerie enters under your control, she exiles the top two cards of a target opponent's library, letting you cast one exiled spell each turn for free if its mana value is equal to or less than your Elf and Faerie count.

articles.title: Digital Extremes says Warframe's imminent Tau update is practically big enough to be a sequel as it reveals new details, including dog walking
articles.summary: Warframe 's latest devstream has just gone live, revealing more about the new Tau solar system players will be able to explore as part of December's "massive" new update, which arrives on 9th December.
body: In a press pre-briefing ahead of the Devstream, Warframe creative director Rebecca Ford and community director Megan Everett discussed the scale of the Tau update, revealing just how much of an ambitious undertaking it's been for the team. "This is a huge update, it is massive," Ford said. "It is a second solar system... Alone, by now, this would have been Warframe two. We're just going for it: we're building a new solar system brick-by-brick."

That begins with a "two-hours-ish" story quest, according to Ford, but there's plenty more besides. Tau brings a new navigation system, for instance, and will feature two playable regions at launch. The World-Seeder Oasis is one: full of environmental hazards, thanks to damaging terraforming efforts, and various missions to complete. Here, players can go bug-collecting for an NPC called Catulast. Doing so increases your standing with him, and provides new rewards.

articles.title: After drawing ire for selling new Mass Effect merch following BioWare closure, EA is now flogging new Dragon Age tat too
articles.summary: Seemingly unperturbed by the criticism it faced after selling new Mass Effect merchandise following the shock closure of developer BioWare, EA is now flogging new merchandise for the studio's other big series, Dragon Age.
body: EA's decision to close BioWare and cancel the long-awaited Mass Effect 5 in October was met with shock and condemnation from fans and games industry veterans alike. Legendary designer Warren Spector slammed the closure, and fan efforts to save the studio - including calls of support from Mass Effect voice acting talent - have continued in the aftermath.

EA, apparently aware of the potentially poor optics, quickly scrubbed a number of Mass Effect-themed cosmetics from Battlefield, but eyebrows were raised when, just weeks later, new Mass Effect merchandise - including a $175 wearable LED helmet - was released onto its BioWare Gear store on 'N7' day, the annual celebration of BioWare's space series. Unsurprisingly, more criticism followed. As one fan put it at the time, "This is such a bad look".

And now here we are again. EA'S BioWare Gear store has sprung to life once more, this time ( thanks IGN ) to promote a new "Seven Swords of Nightmare" hoodie inspired by BioWare's Dragon Age: Inquisition.

articles.title: The canonical USB microphone is still great, and now a total steal for $70
articles.summary: Blue Yeti USB Microphone: was $99.99 now $69.99 I've used a Blue Yeti for nearly a decade and it would happily serve for a decade more. A classic design, good hardware controls, and zero fuss.
body: The Blue Yeti might be the most popular USB microphone ever made, and you know what, it earned it. At its usual price, this is a great USB microphone. At $69.99 (its lowest price ever), it's simply one of the best bangs for your buck in this category.

The original Blue Yeti released in 2009, and in 17 years it has barely changed. I've had mine for a decade, and as I look around, I'm realizing it is the longest-lasting gadget on my desk. That's because it just works: I plug in, adjust the gain, and my voice comes through clear.

These days there are more advanced microphones than the Yeti, like its official sequel the Yeti 2, and certainly mics that are just as competitively priced. Those are good too, and I encourage you to check out cheaper options (like the $26 Amazon Basics mic that we surprisingly love ) before making any decisions.

articles.title: Yooka-Laylee studio explains upcoming Definitive Edition's absence on Xbox to 'frustrated' fans
articles.summary: Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition is notably skipping Xbox Series X/S consoles, and the studio blames "technical challenges and costs."
body: The Definitive Edition is bringing support for 120fps, revamping the platformer's lighting, updating textures and shadows, and packaging in the Trowzer's Top Tonic Pack DLC next month. But a large question mark hung over the lack of an Xbox version.

"Hi folks, just wanted to say a massive thanks to everyone on here for the support for Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition. The response has BEE-n incredible, and we can't wait for you to experience the game all over again on December 15th," developer Playtonic Games said in a new social media post.

"We are aware of feedback regarding the lack of Xbox Series S/X support, and we just wanted to provide some clarity on the reasoning behind this decision. Bringing Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition to PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 has been an exciting adventure… Unfortunately, we've had to prioritise our efforts given the technical challenges and costs presented in the creation of this updated version of the game and as a result, we are unable to commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future," it continued.

articles.title: Skate is dropping seasons and season passes in favor of 'regular, agile content updates'
articles.summary: A little over a year after EA launched Skate into early access—where it remains—developer Full Circle is removing the seasonal structure that has underpinned the game so far, saying that doing so will give the team "the freedom to launch features earlier in their lifecycle." Skate got off to a bit…
body: Skate got off to a bit of a rough start when it went live in September 2025, and while it's turned around the initially iffy response from players, it hasn't gone entirely smoothly since then. An initial promise that no new maps would be locked behind paywalls was chucked out the window in February, and Full Circle laid off employees that same month, saying that cutting headcounts means it can "better support Skate's long-term future and focus the team on the things that matter most to you."

The end of Skate's seasonal structure is less overtly not good than those moves, but it is a sign that things aren't going quite as Full Circle had envisioned, and the message that it's still "committed to keep driving Skate forward" has a certain 'despite everything' tone that doesn't strike me as the sort of thing you say when when all cylinders are firing.

No genre takes this premise quite so literally as the first-person shooter, a pillar of the medium and a fundamental building block of…
There’s no shortage of great first-person shooters, but a select few stand above the rest as high-water marks for the art form.
From pioneers like Doom and Half-Life to multiplayer classics like Counter-Strike and Left 4 Dead 2, here are the 30 First-Person Shooter Masterpieces You Need to Play.
